picks.blurb: Why the Giants Will Beat the Texans, Why They Won’t, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The New York Giants might have a winning record (3-2-1) right now and lead the NFC East. But let’s be honest. Aside from their dominant Week 1 showing against the Dallas Cowboys, have the Giants really looked as good as their record suggests? We’re talking about a team where the phrase “A win’s a win” applies. The Giants barely beat the Tennessee Titans, 12-7, in Week 3. They also had to fight back in Week 4 against the Arizona Cardinals, who led 24-19 at one point. The tie against the Commanders? That one was a gift. If Jayden Daniels and Dan Quinn don’t have that brain blip, the Commanders likely win, despite the Giants roaring back from a 19-6 deficit. And last week? We’re sorry, but the Giants had no business losing to the New Orleans Saints as badly as they did. And again, make no mistake: the Giants lost that game because they were their own worst enemy, as shown by the sloppy play they put on film. But it’s funny how the football gods work. The Giants, regardless of what they do against the Houston Texans this week, will remain in first place in the division. They have a chance, albeit a difficult one, to get back to looking like the team they were in Week 1, even though they’ve since lost a lot of key personnel, all of whom played in that win: quarterback Jaxson Dart, returner/receiver Braxton Berrios, outside linebacker Brian Burns, and inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds. So what’s the goal this week if the Giants want to pull off an upset win over the Texans on the road? “We’ve been practicing well the last few weeks,” head coach John Harbaugh said. “I think practice has been improving every single week, which is the mark of a team that has got a chance to do something. You’ve got to keep improving. “So, we are on track to do that. I’m looking forward to it showing up in terms of consistency. If we’ve been anything, we’ve been inconsistent.” It’s really that simple. The question is, will the Giants finally find the consistency that’s eluded them since that Week 1 game? Why the Giants Will Beat the Texans The Texans might be on a roll, having won their last two games, but they still have a few flaws that could work to the Giants’ advantage. For one, the Texans’ offensive line ranks 27th in the PFF pass-blocking efficiency rating metric. The unit has allowed 71 quarterback pressures, tied for third-most in the league. Left tackle Aireontae Ersery has allowed 20 quarterback pressures, per PFF, tied for fourth-most in the league among left tackles. Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson has turned up the heat on opposing quarterbacks in recent weeks. This year, opposing quarterbacks have completed only 54.1% of their pass attempts against the Giants’ blitz, the fourth-lowest completion rate in the league. Of course, the key is for the Giants to stop the run, something they haven’t done consistently in recent weeks. So we’ll see if Wilson’s calling out his defensive players for not running to the ball lights a fire underneath them. Offensively, the Giants need to get their running game going, and the hope is that switching to quarterback J.J. McCarthy will help. This more mobile quarterback will discourage the Texans from loading up the box and start accounting for McCarthy as a runner. More importantly, McCarthy’s ability to scramble away from trouble could help the Giants’ ailing offensive tackles, Andrew Thomas and, if he plays, Jermaine Eluemunor, against that Texans pass rush. Per Next Gen Stats, since 2025, McCarthy has scrambled 19 times for 185 yards and three touchdowns, a 9.7 yards-per-carry average, which is a league high among quarterbacks with a minimum of 15 carries. If McCarthy can buy time, he stands a chance at connecting with receiver Malik Nabers or tight end Isaiah Likely, both of whom have been the most frequently targeted players on offense for the Giants over the last few weeks. Why the Giants Will Lose to the Texans I touched on it a bit above, but I’ll say it again here. The Giants have to stop the run. Texans’ top running back, David Montgomery, has been sidelined with a groin injury, but Woody Marks has stepped up in his place. Marks is an explosive running back who has averaged almost four yards per rush over the last two weeks. He also has six catches for 47 yards over that span. The Giants’ run defense? Not good at all. Big Blue has allowed opponents 135.5 rushing yards per game this year, and their 5.0 yards per carry allowed is the second-worst average in the league. If the Giants can’t stuff Marks and the Texans’ running game, it won’t matter what pass-rush plan they have this week. And until the unit shows it has cleaned up the missed tackles (13 last week, seven against the run per PFF), that aspect of the game will remain the team’s Achilles heel. At the start of the season, I had this game down as a loss and nothing — not even the Texans’ 2-4 record or the Giants’ 3-2-1 start — has changed my mind. The Texans have been coming into their own lately, and the Giants, aside from their Week 1 win over Dallas, have barely gotten by in their other wins and in their tie against Washington. The Giants will fight — that much I am certain of — and I hope this doesn’t turn into the ugly rout that I fear it could become. After a 0-4 start to the season, Houston got back on track with a 26-3 win in Tennessee, and then a 34-31 win over the Jaguars in London last week. On the other hand, the Giants haven’t won a game since starting the season 3-1. Of course, they played to a tie in Washington before falling 34-27 at home to the Saints last week. Using the latest odds and analysis, here’s where I’m leaning for this Week 7 matchup with a final score prediction. Giants vs. Texans Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Giants +10.5 (-112) Texans -10.5 (-108) 42.5 (Over -118/Under -102) Line Movement: The spread has moved an important point since the odds opened for this game, going from -9.5 to -10.5. The total has also moved by a point, going down from 43.5 to 42.5. Giants vs. Texans Final Score Prediction SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan broke down this game in his Road to 272 Bets column, in which he picks each game every week: Giants vs. Texans Prediction The No. 1 thing that immediately sticks out to me when it comes to these two teams in their difference in their strengths of schedule. Sure, the Texans may be 2-4, and the Giants are 3-2-1, but the Texans have had the sixth most difficult schedule so far this season, with games against the likes of the Bills, Bengals, Cowboys, and Jaguars. Meanwhile, the Giants have had the third-easiest schedule in the league with games against the Titans, Cardinals, Commanders, and Saints. The Houston offense continues to look like a completely different unit as long as Nico Collins remains healthy. Its defense has had a slow start, but I still have faith they'll be one of the best defenses in the NFL for the rest of the way. They'll be able to put the Giants' quarterback in a blender, no matter who it ends up being on Sunday. I don't mind laying the points on Houston. Pick: Texans -9.5 (-110) via BetRivers The Texans are clearly the better overall team than the Giants, despite their records, as MacMillan mentioned, but I think I still need to see an impressive win before I can lay double-digit points. Sure, the Texans blew out the Titans 26-3 two weeks ago, but the Giants are better than Tennessee, and New York’s only blowout loss came in a game where they lost Jaxson Dart early on. picks.blurb: Texans' Week 7 Odds Point to Potential Blowout vs. Giants, J.J. McCarthy Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Houston Texans head into their Week 7 contest against the New York Giants riding the high of logging two straight wins over their last two matchups, and now hope to extend that streak to three in their last game before the bye. And the pieces could certainly be in place for the Texans to make that third consecutive win become a reality. Their offense is looking the best it has all season after another strong performance from C.J. Stroud. The defense will have the task of facing a new starting quarterback on the other side in J.J. McCarthy , and all of that coming back on Houston's home field tends to make their chances look even better. And when looking at the Texans' betting odds heading into Week 7, it's becoming pretty clear that the sportsbooks have one obvious favorite in mind for this weekend's action in Houston. Texans Already Projected to Rout the Giants in Week 7 According to recent odds from FanDuel Sportsbook , the Texans are now listed as 10.5-point favorites (-550 ML) over the Giants in Week 7. That's by far the Texans' highest spread heading into any week they've played this season. And when looking around the league's Week 7 matchups, Houston is currently the only team listed as a favorite by more than a touchdown––let alone being a favorite by double digits. Stroud (7) celebrates his touchdown with wide receiver Nico Collins (12) against the Tennessee Titans during the second half at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The projected point-total for these two teams doesn't look favorable for the Giants either. Houston and New York have an over-under sitting at 43.5, which comes in tied for bottom-five among the NFL in terms of projected totals for Week 7. The projected point-total for these two teams doesn't look favorable for the Giants either. Houston and New York have an over-under sitting at 43.5, which comes in tied for bottom-five among the NFL in terms of projected totals for Week 7. So if the Texans are projected to win by double-digits, and the total score isn't expected to reach above 43 points, that's not much of an optimistic statement from the books on how this Giants offense could fare against a Houston defensive unit that many considered among the best in the NFL heading into this season. Will the Texans Actually Dominate the Giants as Expected? Now, projections are one thing. Clearly, the consensus is starting to lean in one clear direction for this one between the Texans and the Giants. But does Houston actually have what it takes to make that double-digit victory come to fruition? Really, it all relies upon the defense. Last game against the Jacksonville Jaguars showed that the Texans' offense is starting to get into a bit of a rhythm . A ton of receivers are getting involved and making plays, the run game showed signs of life against one of the best rushing defenses in the NFL, and the offensive line even held up to zero sacks. But the Texans' defense just hasn't been as consistently elite as this team proved to be last year. That's not saying they can't find their way back to that level–– because the personnel looks virtually identical to last year outside of a select few changes. But we still need to see Houston have multiple strong weeks defensively to really have this level of confidence in their chances on Sunday. After all, the Giants have won three games as is this season. That's more than the Texans can claim for themselves, and New York sits atop the NFC East because of it. So as 10.5-point underdogs, they seem just a slight bit underrated here, simply when considering Houston's inconsistencies on defense. Maybe the Texans wind up crushing those projections anyways, but perhaps the Giants can make this game just a little bit more interesting than the odds tend to show. Tracy's earliest opportunity to return to the field is a Week 13 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers. The New York Giants got their running game back on track in Sunday's Week 7 win over the Houston Texans, rushing for 188 yards on the road. Each of the Giants' three running backs — Tyrone Tracy Jr., Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary — notched a rushing touchdown in the victory. "We're going to put Tyrone Tracy on IR," Giants general manager Joe Schoen told reporters on Tuesday. In a corresponding move, the Giants signed running back Greg Desrosiers off the Los Angeles Chargers' practice squad. Tracy had 15 yards and one touchdown on six carries in Sunday's win over the Texans. Skattebo led the way with 124 yards and a touchdown on 17 carries, while Singletary capped off the game with a game-winning touchdown run in overtime. The Giants, who lead the NFC East with a 4-2-1 record, now enter their Week 8 bye.

away.headline: Giants Place RB Tyrone Tracy Jr. on IR; Add Former Chargers Runner to Roster
away.blurb: Taking Tracy’s spot on the 53-man roster is running back Greg Desrosiers, whom the Giants signed off the Chargers’ practice squad. Desrosiers, 5-foot-11 and 200 pounds, signed with the Chargers as an undrafted free agent out of Memphis after this year’s draft. Another week, another New York Giants player is heading to injured reserve. Running back Tyrone Tracy Jr., who injured his hamstring in the second quarter of Sunday’s game against the Houston Texans, will be placed on IR this week, general manager Joe Schoen announced ahead of his annual bye-week press briefing. Tracy, the team’s fifth-round draft pick in 2024, has appeared in all seven games this season without making a start. He has 19 rushing attempts for 55 yards and two touchdowns and has caught five of seven targets for 54 yards and a touchdown. He was looking to record his third straight season with 1,000 scrimmage yards, but that goal now appears to be a long shot. Desrosiers had a six-year college career, playing two seasons each for Louisville, Massachusetts and Memphis. He finished with 211 carries for 1,302 yards and 16 touchdowns, and 76 receptions for 612 yards and seven touchdowns as a receiver. This past summer, Desrosiers appeared in all three preseason games for the Chargers, rushing for 166 yards on 23 carries with one touchdown and catching one of two targets for eight yards. McFadden was a full-time starter for the Giants in 2023 and 2024. In Game 1 last season, McFadden suffered a foot injury that kept him out for the remainder of the season. He admitted that “without a doubt” it isn’t easy to no longer have a starting role. “Whenever you’re used to something, you’ve had a taste of the pie, I guess, and then you don’t get to go out there and eat with your boys anymore, it’s tough, but I think it’s just about staying present,” McFadden said. “This game is a week-to-week basis, and obviously I had a pretty upsetting first week last year, and I learned a lot through that process, though. Meanwhile, the Arizona Cardinals may be 2-4, but they're coming off a huge divisional victory over the Los Angeles Rams. The Cardinals are feeling it right now, and they're at home — but we know how Broncos Country travels, especially in the desert. At 4-2, the Broncos can't afford a slip-up — not if they want to keep pace with the Kansas City Chiefs in the division, and make their Week 8 rematch at Mile High a potential chance to get back to the top of the division, depending on what happens this Sunday with the Seattle Seahawks. That's me looking past the Cardinals a little bit. The Broncos won't be doing that. Sean Payton knows how to keep a team's focus on whichever game and opponent is up next, and that's the Cardinals. How will this one shake out? Let's go around the table to see how the Denver Broncos On SI / Mile High Huddle staff see Sunday's action unfolding in Glendale, AZ. Keith Cummings ( @KeithC_NFL ) 4-2 : Getting Bo Nix back in the flow of things has become like a quest for the Holy Grail. All the internal tinkering on Nix might not be as important as facing a Cardinals team the Broncos should beat. While most eyes will be focused on how Nix performs, it's returning rookie running back Jonah Coleman who steals the limelight with two scores. Pick : Broncos 31, Cardinals 21 Chad Jensen ( @ChadNJensen ) 4-2 : The Broncos' coaches and players are buzzing about a Nix breakout game. Looking at the Cardinals' 31st-ranked scoring defense — a unit allowing 350.5 yards per game — this is about as golden a get-right opportunity Nix could hope for. Courtland Sutton said , "At some point, the tide's going to turn" for Nix and this offense, and it happens at State Farm Stadium on Sunday. Nix passes for three touchdowns and 280 yards, while the Broncos romp in the desert. Pick : Broncos 27, Cardinals 17 Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 4-2 : Only speaking for myself, the Broncos haven’t yet earned the benefit of the doubt. Not yet. But if there’s any way to earn that — and any day to have a get-right game — it’s Sunday against the Cardinals. This goes for the offense more so than the defense, which has been fantastic of late. If not now for Nix, then when? Go out there and dominate, and those “confidence issues” will miraculously disappear. I foresee a better showing, though maybe not quite the 2018 Kick Your A** blowout. This is an inferior opponent who, quite frankly, the Broncos should handily dispatch. “Should.” Pick : Broncos 30, Cardinals 16 Nick Kendell ( @NickKendellMHH ) 4-2 : The Broncos' offense has been the source of much consternation. Is Nix hurt? Has the game passed Sean Payton by? Luckily, the Cardinals appear to be a get-right game. It's the NFL; there is no such thing as a guaranteed victory, but I expect the Broncos' defense and special teams, as well as continuity across the organization, to be felt in Arizona. I don't think the offense looks great... and even if it does, it's just one game, and the broader sample size should hold more weight in the total evaluation. Still, it will be nice to provide the fan base some hope. Pick : Broncos 20, Cardinals16 Bob Morris ( @BobMorrisSports ) 4-2 : It's easy to think the Broncos will have their way with the Cardinals. But the Cardinals have shown they can challenge other teams , so it will be important for the Broncos' offense to come out strong. If the Broncos can do that and build a comfortable lead, the defense should be able to finish it from there, even with the Cardinals putting up a fight. Nix has been a shell of himself through six weeks in the 2026 season, yet Denver is somehow 4-2 and favored on the road against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. Arizona is coming off a massive upset win on the road against the Los Angeles Rams, and while it may not be a playoff team, the Cardinals are not a pushover this season. Jacoby Brissett and Co. will have their work cut out for them against a Denver defense that is one of the best in the NFL. The Bronco offense (29th in success rate) hasn’t been able to get much going during this 4-2 start, but the defense has forced 10 turnovers and is allowing just 5.0 yards per play. The play on that side of the ball has stayed intact even with Pat Surtain II (missed the last two games) and Talanoa Hufanga (missed Week 6) injured. Arizona’s defense is one of the weaker ones that the Broncos have on the schedule, so Sean Payton may look to get his young quarterback going early on Sunday. Will it lead to a Denver win? All season long, the SI Betting team is sharing final score predictions for every NFL game, and we’re hoping it’ll help our readers decide on some spread, moneyline and total bets along the way. Plus, who doesn’t want to get an exact score bet right during the season? Denver is favored on the road, but can bettors trust this offense with Nix struggling? This spread suggests we could see a close game, so let’s dive right into my score prediction for this Week 7 battle. Broncos vs. Cardinals Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Broncos -4.5 (-110) Cardinals +4.5 (-110) Broncos: -230 Cardinals: +190 43.5 (Over -115/Under -105) This line has held steady since it opened , as the Broncos are still favored on the road by 4.5 points despite Arizona’s win over the Rams in Week 6. Broncos vs. Cardinals Score Prediction This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan continued his quest to bet on every NFL game in his Road to 272 column . In this matchup, he’s taking Denver to win and cover despite some early struggles on offense: You can throw all of the Broncos' middling metrics out the window, because no team has had a tougher schedule to begin the season than Denver. They've faced the Chiefs, Jaguars, Rams, 49ers, Chargers, and Seahawks, and came out on the other end of that run with a 4-2 record. Despite playing that good a record, their defense still ranks sixth in opponent EPA per play and fifth in opponent success rate. Just imagine how good this defense is going to look when facing lower-tier competition. The Cardinals may be coming off the upset of the year over the Los Angeles Rams, but they enter this week ranking dead last in the NFL in net yards per play at -1.4. Their offense is solid at times, but their defense remains one of the worst units in the league. Give me the Broncos as road favorites. MacMillan has confidence in the Broncos this week, but I’m eyeing the UNDER with the Denver offense looking like one of the worst in the NFL. Arizona’s offense has been able to move the ball with Brissett under center, but Denver has been an elite defense the last few weeks, moving up into the top-12 in the league in points allowed, yards per play allowed, EPA/Play and success rate. The Cardinals are ninth in success rate and 15th in EPA/Play on offense, yet they’ve still scored 21 or fewer points in three of their six games. I expect Brissett to have a much tougher time against a Denver pass defense that – without Pat Surtain II – dominated Seattle and Los Angeles in back-to-back weeks. On the other side of the ball, how can anyone bet on Denver to put up points? The UNDER has hit in five of the Broncos’ six games this season, partially due to the fact that they’ve scored 23 or fewer points in five games and 20 or fewer points in four games. Pictured: Bo Nix, Jacoby Brissett. Stuckey Sun, October 25, 2026 at 7:33 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Denver Broncos (4-2) take on the Arizona Cardinals (2-4) today in NFL Week 7. Kickoff is set for 4:05 p.m. ET from State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Ariz. The game will broadcast live on CBS. The Broncos are 4.5-point favorites on the spread (Broncos -4.5), with the over/under set at 43.5 (-115o / -105u). Denver is a -230 favorite on the moneyline while Arizona is a +190 underdog. Let's get into my Broncos vs Cardinals predictions for Sunday, October, 25. Broncos vs Cardinals pick: Cardinals Moneyline (+176) My Broncos vs. Cardinals best bet is Arizona moneyline (+176), with the best price currently available at FanDuel. Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Download the Action Network app now for more NFL picks and analysis! Broncos vs Cardinals Odds, Lines Broncos vs Cardinals Moneyline: Broncos -230, Cardinals +190 Broncos vs Cardinals Total: 43.5 Broncos vs Cardinals Spread: Broncos -4.5 (-108), Broncos +4.5 (-112) Broncos vs Cardinals Preview Broncos Preview The Broncos are sitting at 4-2, but they are undeniably one of the luckiest teams in the NFL right now. All four of their victories have come by one possession, and their two losses were absolute blowouts. The Broncos easily could have lost to the Seahawks , who doubled them up in total yardage. Denver barely survived a completely broken Chargers team on the road, and needed big comeback efforts against both the Rams and the Jaguars . Bo Nix has been terrible all season. I saw a great stat on X recently: Bo Nix is five letters long, which is basically the same length as his average depth of target (aDOT) — the absolute lowest mark in the NFL. He simply refuses to push the ball downfield. Defensively, Denver is dealing with cluster injuries. The Broncos are likely going to be without both Patrick Surtain and Talanoa Hufanga , completely gutting the back end of their secondary. This could also be a look-ahead spot with the Chiefs on deck. Cardinals Preview The Cardinals are coming off a big win over the Rams, which our Evan Abrams noted was the biggest upset of the season so far with Arizona entering that game as a 12.5-point underdog. Of course, that means we're not buying a bad Cardinals team at the bottom of the market. Still, their offense is capable of exploiting a battered Denver secondary. Marvin Harrison Jr. may be out of the fold, but the Cardinals still have viable weapons in Trey McBride, Michael Wilson, and a reborn Kendrick Bourne. Yes, Arizona's defense isn't very good and consistently gives up points, but it has shown the ability to stay frisky in games and match opponents score for score. With Denver's defense missing its top playmakers in the secondary, Jacoby Brissett should find plenty of open windows. Broncos vs Cardinals Moneyline Pick This is simply me wanting to fade Bo Nix. I am going to force Nix to prove he can actually push the ball down the field and win a game by margin on the road, especially in a potential flat spot with Kansas City looming on deck for the Broncos. Denver has been scraping by against bad teams with improbable late-game variance, and that luck is bound to run out. Give me the Cardinals to win this game outright. away.headline: Cardinals get troubling Jeremiyah Love injury update before Broncos game
away.blurb: Arizona held Love out of last week’s matchup against the Los Angeles Rams, giving the rookie additional time to recover from his ankle injury. For Love, the priority remains getting healthy enough to return without risking another setback. While Arizona has not officially ruled him out for Sunday, the latest report suggests the team may need to prepare for another game without one of its most important young offensive players. Giants DC Threatens Players Amid 'Unacceptable' Behavior, Calls Out 'Traitors' The Arizona Cardinals could be without one of their most promising offensive weapons for another week. Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love is expected to miss Sunday’s matchup against the Denver Broncos as he continues recovering from an ankle injury, according to CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz. Love already missed Arizona ‘s Week 6 victory over the Los Angeles Rams, and the latest report suggests the Cardinals could be forced to play without their starting running back for a second consecutive game. away.headline: Former Denver Broncos Starting QB Released by Buccaneers
away.blurb: Mayfield returned against Carolina on Sunday, October 25, after participating fully in practice leading up to the game. With their starter healthy enough to return, the Buccaneers no longer had the same immediate need for additional quarterback depth. Tampa Bay has not publicly identified Mayfield's return as the reason for Rypien's release. The team elected to use the practice squad opening on Kpeenu, a rookie running back who previously spent time with the Buccaneers during training camp. Rypien began his NFL career with the Broncos as an undrafted free agent out of Boise State in 2019. His release from Tampa Bay does not prevent another NFL team from signing him. As a veteran with starting experience, Rypien remains an available option for a quarterback room in need of additional depth. Former Denver Broncos Starting QB Released by Buccaneers Unlock the latest Heavy on Broncos news — direct to your inbox. Former Denver Broncos starting quarterback Brett Rypien is back on the open market. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers released Rypien from their practice squad on Tuesday, October 27, according to NFL reporter Aaron Wilson, ending his stint with the team less than a month after he arrived. "Buccaneers signed running back Barika Kpeenu to practice squad, released practice squad quarterback Brett Rypien," Wilson reported on X . Rypien, 30, originally joined Tampa Bay on September 30 as the Buccaneers dealt with an injury to starting quarterback Baker Mayfield. His departure comes after Mayfield returned to the lineup against the Carolina Panthers on October 25. For the former Broncos quarterback, it marks another brief stop in a career that has taken him across the NFL since leaving Denver. Brett Rypien Released After Baker Mayfield Returns Rypien's arrival in Tampa Bay was largely a product of the team's quarterback situation. Mayfield suffered a dislocated right thumb against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 3, forcing the Buccaneers to turn to rookie Jalon Daniels. Tampa Bay subsequently signed Rypien to its practice squad, where he joined fellow veteran Easton Stick. The Buccaneers elevated Stick for all three games Mayfield missed, leaving Rypien without a regular-season appearance for Tampa Bay. There was another connection behind the signing. Buccaneers offensive coordinator Zac Robinson previously worked with Rypien when both were with the Los Angeles Rams in 2023, giving the quarterback some familiarity with Tampa Bay's offense. But circumstances have changed. His first NFL start came against the New York Jets on October 1, 2020. Rypien completed 19 of 31 passes for 242 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions in Denver's 37-28 victory. away.headline: Broncos have 8 players on injured reserve going into Week 8
away.blurb: Five of those players — wide receiver Pat Bryant ( ankle ), offensive tackle Frank Crum , tight end Caleb Lohner , running back Tyler Badie ( thumb ) and outside linebacker Jonah Elliss ( ankle ) — are on short-term injured reserve, which means they are eligible to return after four games (although Lohner is expected to be out until at least mid-season ). Bryant will be eligible to return in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers . Badie and Elliss, who just landed on IR over the weekend, will be eligible to return in Week 12. Another player, offensive lineman Nick Gargiulo , is on the reserve/physically unable to perform (PUP) list. He is also eligible to return after four games, but hasn't returned to practice yet. NFL clubs are allowed to designate up to eight players to return from IR each season. Denver has used three of those designations so far this season on Crum, Lohner and running back Jonah Coleman. The rookie running back was activated to the 53-man roster last week, but Crum and Lohner have not yet started their 21-day practice windows. home.headline: Broncos injuries: WR Jaylen Waddle, DL Zach Allen injured vs. Cardinals
home.blurb: Waddle initially stayed down on the field before walking to the sideline and then into the locker room. He was previously limited in two days of practice last week with a chest injury. Denver announced Waddle as questionable to return, but he did not return to Sunday's game after totaling four catches for 48 yards prior to the injury. Elsewhere on the injury front, cornerback Pat Surtain ( ankle ) missed his third straight game on Sunday and safety Talanoa Hufanga ( ankle ) sat out his second consecutive game. After the win, Surtain said, "Not really," when asked by the Denver Gazette 's Chris Tomasson if he was close to playing in Arizona. When asked if he'll play against the Chiefs on Sunday, Surtain said, "Possibly." Denver's first injury report of the week will come out on Wednesday. Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle ( chest ) and defensive lineman Zach Allen ( appeared to be hamstring ) both went down with injuries in the fourth quarter. Waddle suffered his injury after falling on his own fumble on an end-around . After the game, coach Sean Payton called it a " dumb reverse call ." Payton apologized for the "awful" call in his post-game press conference. Allen also went down in the fourth quarter and appeared to be favoring his right hamstring. After a visit to the team's blue medical tent, Allen was spotted standing on the sideline without his helmet for the end of the game. Allen went to the podium for a post-game press conference after the win and said, "Yeah, I'll be fine. Yeah, I'll be good," when asked about his injury. The Packers, winners of three in a row, are coming off a 23-13 defeat of the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football. Meanwhile, Detroit, which spent Week 6 on its bye, defeated the Arizona Cardinals in Week 5, 45-21. Without further ado, here are the predictions from the Detroit Lions On SI staff for the Lions' Week 7 matchup with Green Bay. Christian Booher The Lions have their first chance to prove themselves in the NFC North Sunday, taking on a Green Bay Packers team that appears to be built to exploit Detroit's biggest weakness. Quarterback Jordan Love has been unafraid to test defenses down the field with wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. As a result, I think the Lions will try to dial up the pass-rush and try to get to Love before he has a chance to cut it loose. Offensively, the Lions need to get Jahmyr Gibbs going as the Packers did a good job of keeping him in check in their two meetings last year. Quarterback Jared Goff has been turnover-free through five games, and will need to keep that going to give his team the best chance to win. While the Lions have the ability to keep up in the event this game becomes a shootout, the Packers are uniquely equipped to attack the Lions' issues in coverage, both in the secondary and at linebacker. Green Bay makes one more play than Detroit, and hands Dan Campbell's team a crushing loss to start a crucial two-game stretch. Packers 31, Lions 28 The Detroit Lions have a big time test ahead of themselves on Sunday against the Green Bay Packers. The Packers not only are red hot and winners of three in a row. But they're also due to receive a big boost to their run game with the return of Pro Bowl back Josh Jacobs. In addition, Green Bay receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are playing some of the best football of their NFL careers. Consequently, Kelvin Sheppard's defense won't have it easy in this Week 7 divisional affair. Yet, the Lions' defense will be in the best shape it's been all season due to the return of Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch. He should provide a major boost to the team's secondary and put it in a stronger position to limit the productivity of Watson and Golden. I think Detroit's pass defense holds up just enough and Jared Goff and the offense come through in the fourth quarter, leading Dan Campbell's squad to its fourth victory of the season. Lions 31, Packers 24 John Maakaron The Lions return to action after a much needed week off. The Packers are visiting Ford Field missing a few key players, but will have running back Josh Jacobs in the lineup. If the defensive line can have another strong performance, Jordan Love will not have ample time to find his key targets. Tight end Tucker Kraft could be in line for a big game, but Detroit’s offense should keep the momentum from the first quarter of the season rolling. Sam LaPorta might just also have himself a productive afternoon, given the noise he created and wanting to prove he deserves a lucrative new contract. Emmett Matasovsky The Lions start divisional play with the Green Bay Packers this week, and it sees the return of Brian Branch and Josh Jacobs for their respective teams. That makes this week even more intriguing. It will be interesting to see how, or if, the bye week has given Detroit time to somewhat fix its porous secondary. The return of Branch will give fans a glimpse as to how this secondary should operate, but the boundary corner issues could make this discussion irrelevant. Green Bay is a hard team to gauge, even before factoring in the wild card element that it is a divisional game in the NFC North. picks.blurb: Packers-Lions Prediction: Will Green Bay Beat Odds So It Can Beat Rivals? Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI DETROIT – One of the biggest games of the season for the Green Bay Packers comes with one of the biggest scheduling mismatches imaginable. The Packers are coming off a Sunday night home game. The Lions are coming off a Sunday at their homes with their bye week. So, Detroit – in a huge NFC North game, mind you, that could have playoff ramifications – has been given by the league a home game and a week of rest. Will it matter? Here are our predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Lions Prediction Since the start of the 2020 season, teams with a home game after their bye are 63-41, according to Stathead. That’s an enormous advantage. Will that alone decide the game? Probably not. But in a game between two quality teams – the Lions are 3.5-point favorites – it might not take much to be the tipping point. Eight consecutive games at Ford Field between the teams ended with a one-score differential; the last exception was in 2017, when Brett Hundley was the Packers’ quarterback. Both teams are going to score points. A lot of points. The over/under of 55.5 points is the highest on the board at FanDuel. The Lions on offense have been a well-oiled machine. It tallied 30 points in five of six games this season and is second in the league in scoring. Quarterback Jared Goff hasn’t thrown an interception all season. He is surrounded by probably the best quartet in the league with receivers Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams, running back Jahmyr Gibbs and tight end Sam LaPorta. Green Bay’s defense was great last week against the Dak Prescott-led Cowboys passing attack, but it didn’t have to contend with a back like Gibbs, who is arguably the best in the league – especially at home. The Packers have been hit and miss on offense – which is about what you’d expect for a team with a big-time quarterback and two big-play receivers but with an inconsistent offensive line and an unimaginably bad running game. The matchup is favorable, though, because the Lions’ defense has been terrible. It ranks 30th in points allowed and 32nd in total defense. At its current clip, it will threaten the 2011 Packers as the worst pass defense in NFL history. For the Lions, the best defense has been a good offense. They are 3-2 despite allowing 20 touchdowns. According to Stats Perform’s Opta data, they are the first team in NFL history to allow 20 offensive touchdowns and have a winning record through five games. Ultimately, three big issues stand the Packers’ way. One, they have struggled to protect Love. Well, the Lions lead the NFL in sacks even while playing one fewer game than most teams. Can Green Bay’s tackles overcome the noise to keep Aidan Hutchinson away from Love? Two, they have struggled to pressure the quarterback at times. Goff is an elite quarterback when given time. As coach Matt LaFleur said this week, “It’s hard for a quarterback to throw when he’s on his back.” Can the Packers put Goff on his back enough? Furthermore, the Green Bay defense will line up without Micah Parsons, Edgerrin Cooper and Zaire Franklin. And, finally, there’s this festering problem: The Packers have fatal flaws they haven’t solved. Love has been stymied by 19 drops; no other quarterback has more than 11. They lead the league in penalties and penalty yards. Love has faced the third-most pressures. “The simple stuff, whether from scheme-wise or the understanding of what we’re trying to get done, when you have some mistakes that can lead to negative plays, that’s the stuff we got to clean up and be better at,” Love said. It’s those things that will put the Packers at a disadvantage in every big game – no matter the location or scheduling quirk – until they get them fixed. Ultimately, the team that makes the fewest mistakes will win. Based on the first five games, it’s hard to believe that will be the Packers. Bill Huber’s Prediction: Lions 31, Packers 27. Bill’s Record: 3-2. Jacob Westendorf’s Packers-Lions Prediction The Packers have lost too many games like these in recent years, which have caused them to travel the long road in the postseason. In 2024, they lost all but one division game, which played a significant factor in them being the seventh seed in the NFC playoffs. Last year’s late-season debacle in Chicago essentially sealed their fate that the wild-card meeting rematch would be at Soldier Field instead of the friendly confines of Lambeau Field. Simply put, the Packers need to knock off the Lions on the road on Sunday to keep pace with those in front of them and remain in position to be a legitimate NFC North contender. In a game where points should be scored in bunches, one mistake could be the difference. Who do you trust more to play clean and disciplined? Dan Campbell's Lions or Matt LaFleur's Packers? That, combined with the Lions being at home off a bye, gives them the nod. Jacob’s Prediction: Lions 34, Packers 31 Jacob’s Record: 3-3. Most recently, the Matt LaFleur-led squad dispatched of the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football, 23-13. It marked the third consecutive game in which Green Bay held its opponent to 14 or fewer points. And on the season, the Packers’ defense – coordinated by former Arizona Cardinals head coach Jonathan Gannon – has allowed the 10th-fewest points in the NFL (20.8/game). Meanwhile, on the opposite side of the ball, Green Bay – led under center by sixth-year passer Jordan Love – has scored the 10th-fewest points in the game (21.2/game). Through six weeks, Love has also completed just 59.7 percent of his pass attempts. If the season ended today, it'd rank as his lowest completion percentage as a starting quarterback in the NFL. Yet, multiple Green Bay pass-catchers have flourished, most notably wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Watson, now in his fifth NFL season, has already amassed as many touchdowns as last season (six) and nearly as many receptions (29) and reception yards as he did a year ago (538). The former second-round pick secured 35 catches and 611 yards in 10 games a season ago. Meanwhile, Golden, Green Bay's first-round pick in 2025, has already surpassed all his receiving totals from his rookie campaign. He's already racked up 30 catches, 501 yards and three touchdowns amid a career breakout season. And just like Watson, he's well on pace for a 1,000-yard receiving campaign. Consequently, both Watson and Golden possess the potential to wreak havoc against the Lions’ secondary, even with Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch back in the fold for Detroit. In addition to Watson and Golden, the Lions will also likely have their hands full with Packers running back Josh Jacobs. The Pro Bowler returns to the lineup after spending the first six weeks of the season on the commissioner exempt list for an offseason domestic abuse incident. Jacobs, who's coming off a 929-yard, 13-touchdown rushing campaign in 2025, should provide an immediate boost to Green Bay's league-worst ground game. In case you were wondering, the Packers have compiled a measly 359 total rushing yards through the season's first six games. Expect Jacobs, along with Watson and Golden, to give Kelvin Sheppard's defense its fair share of fits on Sunday. However, at this present juncture, I'm still willing to give the Lions a 60 percent chance to pull off the Week 7 victory at home. away.headline: Packers injury report: Jordan Love upgraded, 2 defensive starters added
away.blurb: Love, who is dealing with back soreness coming out of last Sunday's win over the Dallas Cowboys, got in a full padded practice on Thursday. He said Wednesday that he had no concerns over his availability for Sunday's showdown with the Detroit Lions , and Love's upgraded practice status on Thursday appears to confirm his belief. Barring a setback, he'll start against the Lions at Ford Field. Two defensive starters are dealing with new issues: Franklin has a shin injury, while Van Ness has an illness. It's currently unclear if either player is in danger of missing Sunday. More information will be available come Friday, when Matt LaFleur answers questions from the media before practice and before the Packers release a final injury report. Last week, safety Evan Williams was able to get through an illness and play well against the Cowboys. The only player who did not participate for the Packers at practice on Thursday was receiver Bo Melton, who is dealing with a back injury. He can be assumed out for Sunday unless he practices in some capacity on Friday. Receivers Christian Watson (ankle) and Matthew Golden (shoulder) both practiced in a limited capacity. LaFleur said both would play Sunday against the Lions. Limited participation: LG Aaron Banks (knee/toe), DL Anthony Campbell (ankle), CB Brandon Cisse (shoulder/neck), LB Zaire Franklin (shin), WR Matthew Golden (shoulder), DL Jordon Riley (Achilles), CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), EDGE Lukas Van Ness (illness), WR Christian Watson (ankle), WR Savion Williams (ankle) Packers updated Week 7 injury report, Thursday Full participation: QB Jordan Love (back) Did not participate: WR Bo Melton (back) A final injury report for both teams will arrive on Friday afternoon. away.blurb: The Packers didn’t designate Micah Parsons for return this week because the team doesn’t actually practice this week, which would mean one-third of his 21-day return-to-play window would have been wasted. Receiver Matthew Golden (shoulder and foot) did not practice. Along with Christian Watson, Golden is the driving force in the passing game. Without him, the Packers would be incredibly shorthanded in terms of passing-game playmakers. There was some good news, though. Defensive tackles Devonte Wyatt (ankle) and Anthony Campbell (ankle) would not have practiced on Monday but would have been limited on Tuesday. Campbell was one of the standouts against Detroit. Still a DNP was Phillips, who signed a four-year, $120 million contract in free agency this past offseason. He has 2.5 sacks in five games but was inactive last week against Tampa Bay. Packers-Lions Final Injury Report: Zaire Franklin Out; Backups Thrown Into Fire GREEN BAY, Wis. – As is typically the case for a Thursday night game, the Green Bay Packers will be a banged-up bunch for their game against the Carolina Panthers. The Packers held a walk-through practice on Tuesday. If they would have practiced, they would have been down four starters. One of them was Travis Glover, who has started the past four games at right guard. More on that and the injury report in a moment. But first, there was a potential big update on the status of Micah Parsons. “I sure hope so,” coach Matt LaFleur said on Wednesday evening. There was a touch of optimism there, though LaFleur was quick to remind that it will be a medical decision before the superstar pass rusher returns to practice. “I’m itching for it, though, for sure,” LaFleur said. Will Kevin Zeitler Start at Right Guard? Glover is dealing with a knee injury and didn’t play particularly well against the Lions. If he’s not ready, will Kevin Zeitler make his long-awaited debut? Zeitler was inactive against Detroit and has played only on special teams in his two appearances. “If we need him, absolutely,” LaFleur said when asked if Zeitler is ready to contribute on offense. “I think he's done a nice job. Here's a guy that came in and didn't have an offseason, didn't have training camp, and he's kind of gradually working his way back into it.” Good News and Bad News for Packers Linebacker Zaire Franklin would not have practiced due to the shin injury sustained at practice last week and will not be ready for Thursday, LaFleur said. That means a secon consecutie week for Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper. “I sure hope so,” LaFleur said when asked about Golden’s availability, “but we're still kind of working through it. You're not getting any real reps. Everything's pretty much walk-through. We will have a short indy [individual drills period] tomorrow, but to move guys around and see how they look, but certainly hopeful for him.”

away.headline: Packers rule out Zaire Franklin, list four questionable vs. Lions | Week 7 Injury Report
away.blurb: Packers rule out Zaire Franklin, list four questionable vs. Lions | Week 7 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News Evan Siegle, packers.com LB Zaire Franklin GREEN BAY – Packers have officially ruled out linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin) and listed four questionable for Sunday's NFC North matchup with the Detroit Lions. The four questionable are guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), receiver Bo Melton (back) and defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles), who's currently on the physically unable to perform list and would need to be added to the 53-man roster to play against the Lions. Sunday will mark only the second game Franklin has missed in nine NFL seasons, snapping a streak of 48 consecutive games played dating back to Week 8 of the 2023 season when the former All-Pro linebacker sat out against Carolina with a knee injury. The Packers could have reinforcements on the way up front against the Lions and star running back Jahmyr Gibbs, as Riley appears to be nearing a return. The third-year defensive tackle has practiced in a limited capacity the past two weeks, his first on-field work since tearing his Achilles last December. Banks has been out since injuring his toe against the New York Jets in Week 2. The 6-foot-5, 325-pound guard was also battling knee tendinitis at the time of his toe injury. home.headline: Detroit Lions sign former Vikings DL to practice squad, release WR
home.blurb: Originally an undrafted free agent by the Vikings in 2024 out of Oregon , Taimani finished with 22 tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, one quarterback hurry, and one fumble recovery during the 2023 college football season with the Ducks. As Sunday's NFC North showdown approaches, the Detroit Lions (4-2) signed former Minnesota Vikings (6-0) defensive lineman Taki Taimani to their practice squad on Tuesday. Taimani, a 6-foot-1, 309-pound lineman, has appeared in nine NFL games (all with the Vikings ) and has registered four tackles. Per Pro Football Focus , Taimani logged 70 defensive snaps in 2024 and carded a 61.2 overall defensive grade that season. In 2025, Taimani tallied just 35 defensive snaps and had an overall defensive grade of 27.4 last season from PFF . In its corresponding move, the Lions released wide receiver Lawrence Keys from their practice squad. Detroit signed Keys back in June after a stint in the UFL with the Houston Gamblers. The 5-foot-11, 170-pound receiver finished second in the UFL with 1,001 all-purpose yards over the Gamblers' 10-game schedule. Keys registered 349 receiving yards on 24 receptions including two touchdown catches. The 26-year-old also returned 19 kickoffs for 518 yards and 11 punts for 134 yards and a 12.2 average, which ranked third in the league. After going undrafted in 2024, Keys signed with the Buffalo Bills . But, he was released prior to the start of the 2024 NFL season. During his college career at Notre Dame and then Tulane, Keys caught 81 passes for 1,080 yards and nine touchdowns. Keys' most productive collegiate season was 2023 when he hauled in 30 passes for 296 yards and two scores. Keys was waived by the Lions in August during training camp with an injury settlement before signing back onto the practice squad in late September. Well, anyone backing the Raiders in Week 7 has a lot more company, with a good chunk of the experts giving them a real shot against the Rams Sunday at Allegiant Stadium. Covering the spread against Buffalo apparently buys a team some respect. The computer models still like the Rams comfortably, but some of the humans are far less sure, and a few of them switched sides from last week. Even the Raiders Wire staff is on board too, picking the Raiders 3-1 with an average score of 27-25. NFL.com's panel can barely agree Three of NFL.com's five analysts picked the Rams, with Jeremy Bergman at 24-17, Gennaro Filice at 27-24 and Dan Parr at 31-27. The other two went with the Raiders, and both picks come with a story. Bobby Kownack had the Bills hanging 35 points on the Raiders last week. Now he has the Raiders winning a 17-14 rock fight , which is quite a change of heart in seven days. Brooke Cersosimo has the Raiders by one at 25-24, and the Rams clearly gave her more to think about than she expected. "Of all the teams in the league, I would not have guessed the Rams would give me pause at this point in the season," Cersosimo wrote. She also has the game ending on a Raiders field goal in the final minute. Bleacher Report's experts traded seats The funniest twist came from Bleacher Report. Maurice Moton was the panel's lone Raiders backer last week, and this week he jumped to the Rams, while Gary Davenport, who doubted the Raiders against Buffalo, came over to their side. "Why lay this many points on the road against a Raiders team that just covered the same spread against Buffalo?" Davenport wrote. Moton expects the Rams to adjust without Davante Adams by leaning on their tight ends. The panel finished 4-3 in favor of the Raiders against a 4.5-point spread, with Ian Hanford, Wes O'Donnell and Brent Sobleski joining Davenport. Pete Prisco and Mike Florio keep it tight CBS Sports' Pete Prisco picked the Rams to win by a single point, 28-27, which is a polite way of taking the Raiders against the spread. "They still have Matt Stafford. He can light up a defense, which he will do here," Prisco wrote. "But the Rams will give up some big plays to the Raiders, who hang around." The rest of the CBS panel split 4-3 for the Rams against the spread, with Tyler Sullivan and Jamey Eisenberg standing with Prisco. Meanwhile, Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio has the Rams winning 26-23 and sees a season on the line for Los Angeles. "If the Rams get to five losses with 10 games left, they could be done," Florio wrote. The computers aren't buying it The models are far more confident than we (humans). Dimers gives the Rams a 70.8% chance to win with a 26-20 projection, and the Covers AI model has Los Angeles winning 27-20. Five of the seven human score predictions in this roundup land within three points, though. These experts expect another one-score game, and the Raiders have lost two of their last three games by a field goal. And the Raiders have a major concern as well. These teams meet in Week 7, and here are bold predictions for the NFL contest. It's a crucial game for the Rams, who stand at 2-4 and find themselves a staggering four games behind the front-running 49ers in the NFC West. Meanwhile, the Raiders stand at 3-3 in third place in the AFC West. They're unlikely to be a playoff contender, but are trying to build a strong foundation for 2027. Let's take a look at what could happen when these teams battle. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Matthew Stafford will throw for three touchdowns It's hard to gauge what kind of yardage output Stafford will have. Without the injured Davante Adams, the Rams may lean on the ground game a little more. Adams is the team's leading receiver with 480 yards and four touchdowns. Sure, Stafford still has Puka Nacua. And Nacua will get his targets and yardage. But who steps into the No. 2 role? Maybe the Rams will use tight end Tyler Higbee more. Or perhaps Konata Mumpfield or Jordan Whittington will step up and produce. However, despite the receiver situation, the Rams will need to find a way to get the ball into the end zone if the Raiders load up to stop the run in the red zone. So look for Stafford to spread it around and still get his TD passes. Stafford said he understands the situation , according to The Athletic. "I just feel even more responsibility to try to be as good as I can be to help us continue to win," Stafford said. "In some of those guys' instances where they're going to have opportunities to hopefully come back and play for us, make sure that when they come back and play for us, it's meaningful stuff for them." However, some observers think Stafford has finally reached the end of his NFL rope, according to ESPN. "Stafford can't move," Ben Solak wrote. "He was never the most mobile quarterback, but the Rams were willing to use him on boots in the past. In 2024, 16.8% of Stafford's pass attempts were on the run — an above-average number! That fell to 13.9% in 2025 and is down to 9.6% in 2026. Sure, designed rollouts are down — but it isn't just that. "Stafford has zero scrambling passing yards on the season per NFL Next Gen Stats. He has yet to break the pocket and complete a pass on a scramble drill. The last quarterback to log no scramble passing yards through six weeks of a season was 2022 Tom Brady — the final season of a pocket passing titan." But it's not time to write Stafford off. Rams RB Kyren Williams will rush for 90-plus yards The Rams must run the football against the Raiders, a team that struggles to stop the ground game. The Raiders are giving up 134.3 yards per game, which ranks No. 28 in the NFL. Keeping the ball on the ground needs to be a big part of the Rams' game plan. The Rams have thrown 252 passes with 148 rushing attempts. McVay wants those numbers closer together , according to theramswire.com. "Ultimately, what I care about and what we care about is what's the best way is to move the ball and score points," McVay said. "Because of some of the situations that we've been in, those two-minute situations have gotten us a little bit out of balance. No matter how I cut it, it's an excuse. I'd like to be able to have a little bit more balance. And that's reflected by being efficient on early downs and sustaining drives." One thing is for sure, Williams and the Rams haven't lost their belief that this can be a special season. "Man, my confidence is still as high as ever," Williams said. "We know what we've got on our team and in this locker room. We come to practice every single week. That's why we can't lose our focus. We can't lose what matters the most, and that's the work. "It's about having faith. That the work we put in every single week will come to shine." Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty will split carries with Mike Washington Jr. There's no doubt that Jeanty has been a huge disappointment for the Raiders. They picked him No. 6 overall, expecting a franchise-changing player. Instead, Jeanty has a career average of 3.5 yards per carry. And Washington has been turning heads with the coaching staff, according to a post on the Raiders' YouTube page via Athlon Sports. But he needs to be better at pass protection . "He's a rookie, so he had a lot to catch up on," Kubiak said when asked about Washington's role in the passing game. "He's continuing to improve. (And) he's putting the work in. You see the practice come to life in the games. He's not where he wants to be. He's got to keep growing." Jeanty has been a threat in the passing game. Maybe his future is as a third-down back. Washington could supplant him. And the prediction is for that to begin this week. Jeanty has time to bounce back. It's still early in his career. But he simply hasn't been able to show in the NFL what he showed in college. away.headline: Report: Rams WR Puka Nacua's injury not believed to be serious
away.blurb: Oct 23 (Field Level Media) - Rams receiver Puka Nacua sustained a calf injury in practice Thursday that is not expected to be serious, NFL Network reported. Per the report, his status is "up in the air" for the Rams (2-4) for Sunday's road game against the Las Vegas Raiders (3-3). Los Angeles head coach Sean McVay is expected to speak to reporters on Friday. The Rams will be without fellow wideout Davante Adams, who was placed on injured reserve earlier in the week with a ruptured hamstring. The other members of the receiver room are Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Alex Bachman. Nacua, 25, has 37 catches for 417 yards and one touchdown to go with one rushing score in four games this season. He missed two games with a psoas injury. A two-time Pro Bowl selection, Nacua led the NFL with 129 receptions last season and racked up 1,715 receiving yards with 10 touchdowns in 16 games.

away.headline: Rams sign LB Jon Rhattigan, release two practice squad players
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: Rhattigan is a seasoned special teams option with 1,260 snaps on special teams since 2021. He signed with the Seattle Seahawks as an undrafted free agent out of Army in 2021, then spent time with the Carolina Panthers, Pittsburgh Steelers and Las Vegas Raiders. He signed with the Chicago Bears in May and was released on Aug. 30. The Los Angeles Rams are making a small roster shake-up, releasing cornerback Nyzier Fourqurean and linebacker Eli Neal from the practice squad and signing linebacker Jon Rhattigan, according to KPRC 2’s Aaron Wilson . It's unclear if Rhattigan is going to the active roster or practice squad. Fourqurean signed with the Rams as an undrafted free agent after the 2026 NFL draft. Los Angeles waived him as part of final roster cuts on Aug. 30 and re-signed him to the practice squad the next day. Neal, a linebacker, has been with the Rams since he signed as an undrafted free agent in 2024. He made the initial 53-man roster that year and later bounced between waivers, the practice squad and reserve/futures deals. His snaps have come entirely on special teams across 10 career games with no offensive or defensive snaps. Rhattigan has appeared in 65 games over five seasons without a start, totaling 50 tackles. That includes 17 tackles with Seattle in 2023 and 12 with Carolina in 2024. He played 12 games for the Raiders last year. away.headline: Rams' Power Rankings Roundup Has Los Angeles Rising Everywhere as the Run Game Returns
away.blurb: Ralph Vacchiano gave the Rams the biggest jump, four spots, and opened his blurb with a movie line. “Just when I thought I was out, they pull me back in,” he wrote for FOX Sports , crediting Matthew Stafford’s passing and the “two-pronged rushing attack” of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. McDuffie has missed the last two games with a groin injury, but Barshop wrote for ESPN that he’s allowed a 28.6% completion rate in coverage, the best of any player targeted at least 20 times, according to Next Gen Stats. Even with him out, the Rams have stayed top 12 on both sides of the ball by EPA per play. Building a 28-3 lead in Las Vegas was the kind of performance the Los Angeles Rams needed, and the national power rankings noticed. All four major outlets moved the Rams up after their 35-21 win over the Raiders , and two of them pushed L.A. into the top 12. The common thread was the run game. Three of the four write-ups mentioned it, and at 3-4, it might be what decides whether this is a turnaround or another one-week spike. He’s not all the way in. “If only they could put it together for more than one game at a time,” Vacchiano wrote. FOX also noted Stafford’s three touchdown passes made him the franchise leader, a record he joked about after the game . ESPN’s panel moved L.A. up two spots. This week’s list named each team’s best offseason addition, and Sarah Barshop chose cornerback Trent McDuffie, whom the Rams acquired in a trade and made the highest-paid corner in league history at the time. Pete Prisco moved the Rams up two spots and sounded like he’d been waiting for this version all year. “The team we saw beat up the Raiders is the Dream Team we expected to see before the season. The run game is back,” Prisco wrote for CBS Sports . PFT only bumped L.A. a spot, but it landed in the same place. “If they can keep running the ball the way they did on Sunday, they can start stacking wins,” PFT wrote in its rankings . Averaged across the four outlets, the Rams sit at about No. 14, up from roughly No. 16 a week ago. That’s a solid climb for one win, and the winless Chargers come to SoFi Stadium on Sunday. Every Rams loss also helps Cleveland , which owns their 2027 first, so stacking wins matters for more than just the standings. away.headline: Rams get interesting trade report after Davante Adams' multi-week injury
away.blurb: After such a brutal injury, ESPN's Dan Graziano is reporting that the Rams, even at 2-4, are expected to search the WR trade market for potential additions to try and keep their season alive while Adams is out. It wouldn't make sense to give up now, especially since Garrett should come back, and Adams could return later this season as well. Rams get interesting trade report after Davante Adams' multi-week injury | Sporting News Skip to main content SN 140 Watch Watch How to Watch Streaming Services fubo Add Sporting News on Google div))]:my-4" data-testid="advert--mobile_branded_logo" id="Branded_Logo_Mobile"> The 2-4 Los Angeles Rams are one of the most disappointing teams in the NFL this season. Meant to be a top Super Bowl contender, there's a real chance that the Rams aren't even a playoff team when it's all said and done. But their season isn't over yet. However, the team did just get a crushing piece of news following Week 6, as star wide receiver Davante Adams was revealed to have suffered a serious, multi-week hamstring injury. Rams expected to make trade calls for WR help after Davante Adams injury "I do not expect the Rams to go down without a fight, and my understanding is that they will at least explore the possibility of trading for a wide receiver in the wake of Davante Adams' hamstring injury," Graziano reports. This is a noteworthy development for the Rams, as it shows the team is still trying to compete and make the playoffs from their 2-4 record, despite the 6-0 San Francisco 49ers dominating and the NFC Wild Card being a very tight race. But the Rams potentially adding wide receiver help shouldn't come as a huge surprise, as they had already been one of the teams linked to WRs on the trade market, even before the Adams injury. This is an all-in team after their blockbuster trades for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie. Spending a few more draft picks on WR help wouldn't be a surprise whatsoever. They've already mortgaged their future on this 2026 roster. MORE : ESPN analyst believes Browns are a quarterback away from being Super Bowl contenders While the Rams might not land a blockbuster name like Brian Thomas Jr., someone like Jerry Jeudy would be a solid veteran presence in the WR room to help in the meantime while Adams sits on IR with a serious hamstring injury. They're already all-in for 2026; there's no reason why they shouldn't invest a bit more to bolster a roster that can still do some damage if they make the playoffs. Graziano is reporting that WR help is something Les Snead and Sean McVay will consider adding. While the 2-4 Rams might not seem like a buyer, this team is in too deep to not continue striving for a title in 2026. home.blurb: Las Vegas Raiders linebacker Quay Walker has been downgraded to questionable with a chest injury ahead of Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams. The change raises uncertainty about his availability for the Week 7 matchup at Allegiant Stadium. ESPN's Raiders reporter Ryan McFadden reported the downgrade on X on Saturday. Walker had been a full participant in Friday's practice after being limited on Wednesday and Thursday, according to the Raiders' official injury report. The injury report also lists running back Mike Washington Jr. as questionable for Las Vegas with foot and back issues. For Los Angeles, wide receiver Puka Nacua is questionable with a calf injury, while linebacker Nate Landman has been ruled out with a concussion. Walker was limited during the first two practices of the week before completing Friday's session without a game-status designation on the team's published report. The subsequent downgrade means his availability remains uncertain, although the available reporting does not establish whether he experienced a setback or explain the reason for the change. The Raiders host the Rams on Sunday, Oct. 25, with kickoff scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET. Las Vegas will need to clarify Walker's status before the game, while his questionable designation leaves open the possibility that he could still play. home.blurb: Bowers was limited on Wednesday because of hamstring and calf injuries . He missed the first two games of the 2026 season after undergoing a minor knee procedure shortly before the campaign began. His latest injury report designation is the first time this season he has been listed with an issue other than his knee. Bowers' return to full practice participation comes as the Raiders attempt to end a three-game losing streak. Over their past three games, Las Vegas has been outscored 64-41 after halftime, including a 24-3 disadvantage in the third quarter. The Raiders have also committed seven second-half turnovers this season, with four of quarterback Kirk Cousins' five interceptions occurring during the final two quarters. Las Vegas has shown offensive potential, averaging 26.7 points per game, the sixth-highest mark in the league. However, inconsistent red-zone execution and defensive woes have prevented the Raiders from consistently closing out games. Alongside Bowers, defensive tackle Folorunso Fatukasi and offensive tackle Kolton Miller also returned to full participation after being limited Wednesday. Defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway was limited after missing the previous practice, while running back Mike Washington did not participate and linebacker Quay Walker remained limited. Don't let the home team's offensive struggles fool you, though, as this remains one of the premier clubs in the NFL. Head coach Mike Macdonald's group might have the game's best wide receiver in Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and the Seahawks' defense is in the conversation for being football's most elite unit once again. Kansas City has its work cut out for it in what could be a tough road game, but one thing this year's team has shown is an abundance of grit. Will Sunday Night Football be more of the same? How might today's game unfold? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 7 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: Between the Seahawks’ offensive inconsistencies and the Chiefs’ offensive injuries, this feels like a low-scoring, wire-to-wire affair between two teams with elite elements in some areas and significant questions in others. Ultimately, fitting the narrative of the week perfectly, Kenneth Walker should be the key to this game for both teams. Jordan Foote: Going into Seattle and securing a win is easily the toughest ask of the Chiefs through the first month-and-a-half of the season. The Seahawks' defense, even while banged up, is amazing. On the other side of the ball, however, there's next to no run game. That's had a negative impact on quarterback Sam Darnold, who also isn't sniffing the production he found a season ago. Week 7's tilt could go either way, but I'll side with the offense I believe in much more. Minus wideout Rashee Rice and right tackle Jaylon Moore , look for this one to be a statement game for one or both of quarterback Patrick Mahomes and running back Kenneth Walker III in hostile territory. Joshua Schulman: Kenneth Walker is set to return to face the franchise he won a Super Bowl with less than nine months ago, and he'll be looking to make his former team regret letting him walk. He and Jaxon Smith-Njigba headline one of the most exciting Sunday Night Football contests in recent memory. There's a generational quarterback in Patrick Mahomes squaring off against a generational defense that has picked up where it left off a season ago, despite the offense's inconsistencies. Seattle's slow start has actually placed it out of the playoff picture, and a home loss before another prime-time showdown against the Bears would be disastrous. I think the Seahawks understand the importance of this matchup and will take advantage of their 10 days of rest. Given the Chiefs' shaky kicking game and a lack of proven offensive weapons outside of Walker in what should be a low-scoring contest, I think Mike Macdonald and Co. narrowly steal one to hand Kansas City its first loss. Tyler Brown: This one has the look of a defensive rock fight. Seattle’s passing defense ranks first in the NFL, allowing just 141 yards per game, and Kansas City’s defense has held opponents under 20 points in most of its wins. The ingredients are there for a low-scoring grind from start to finish. That said, the Chiefs are the number one offense in the NFL for a reason. Seattle’s defense may be able to slow down Walker or Mahomes, but doing both simultaneously is a different ask entirely. If the run game gets going, the play-action attack opens up. If Mahomes starts finding his receivers, the box opens up for Walker. At some point, one of those two is going to win. On the other side, if Sam Darnold can buy time in the pocket, Smith-Njigba is going to get loose. The Chiefs’ defense just has to make sure that happens once or twice rather than repeatedly. They will compete in a Sunday Night Football matchup for the second time in 2026 as they head to Seattle to take on the reigning Super Bowl champions. While Andy Reid's squad has yet to drop a game, the Seahawks have struggled to get their offense going in the post-Kenneth Walker era . Amid their two-game losing streak, quarterback Sam Darnold has tossed four interceptions, including one that ultimately gave the Broncos a free victory last week in overtime. Walker's homecoming to the team he spent his first four years with is a major storyline. He'll be looking to prove why Seattle should have paid him as he continues to establish himself as one of the best running backs in the NFL. The Chiefs have had plenty of breaks go their way and won't stay undefeated forever, but the Seahawks will have a tough time overcoming turnovers from Darnold if they want to win. away.headline: ‘I don't know if he plays for the Chiefs again' - NFL Insider drops troubling update on Kansas City Chiefs' Josh Simmons days after he lands on IR
away.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
away.blurb: The starting left tackle, Simmons, hasn’t played since mid-August. His only exception was a limited practice week ahead of Kansas City’s Week 6 game against the Los Angeles Chargers. The absence stems from a back injury that has been described as a bulging disc . The Chiefs placed Simmons on injured reserve after VP of Sports Medicine and Performance Rick Burkholder explained the injury . “Things happen,” Reid said . “That’s no reason he was put on IR. He’s got a bad back. He’s got to get that worked out. That’s the main thing.” “So the gist of the report was this: something I reported with Mike Garafolo on Sunday, as you mentioned, that Josh Simmons was asked to leave a team meeting by Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes,” Rapoport said . “It involved having his feet up on the desk. He said he needed to because of his back. He’s going through rehab, and they said, ‘Well, just get out of here and go rehab.’ He did not handle it well. He went and apologized after. “Then he was placed on injured reserve, and there are a lot of questions about Josh Simmons, who has as talented a left tackle as you could possibly get, he is a stud as a player. I don’t know if he plays for the Chiefs again. I don’t know when he plays for the Chiefs again. There’s nothing more important than protecting Patrick Mahomes. You have to believe in the person doing it, and until that happens, I don’t know that he’s out there.” That distinction matters. Teams will stand by a player through injuries and even through odd absences. However, that patience tends to run out once an organization believes the effort isn’t going both ways. That said, the old NFL adage has to matter at some point: Availability is the best ability. Simmons missed nine games in 2025, and he has already missed six more in 2026. That’s 15 missed games out of 23 possible. He’s played in just eight games since being selected with the last pick in Round 1 of the 2025 NFL Draft. He’ll miss at least three more games on injured reserve. So far, there’s been no indication Simmons will return to play in the 2026 NFL season. Perhaps Rapoport is trying to send a message to the young, talented Simmons on behalf of the Chiefs. The Kansas City Chiefs placed LT Josh Simmons on injured reserve after months of questions about his back.
