LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Dallas has dropped two straight games, but Philadelphia enters the NFC East matchup without Jalen Hurts Imagn Images In the Week 7 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Philadelphia Eagles play host to the division rival Dallas Cowboys . Philadelphia has lost four consecutive games after starting the season 2-0, and enters this game ravaged by injuries. Not only is Jalen Hurts out in the wake of blood clots being found in his calf and lungs, but DeVonta Smith , Dontayvion Wicks , Nolan Smith and more will also miss the game, while Saquon Barkley , Landon Dickerson , Jonathan Greenard and Jalyx Hunt are all questionable. Dallas has lost back-to-back games in dispiriting fashion, with its offense sputtering at the worst possible time, combining for 29 points against the Buccaneers and Packers after scoring 30-plus in each of the previous three games. The defense was already under fire early in the season, and now the Cowboys have questions on the side of the ball where they were supposed to be elite. Which of these two teams will stop their losing skid? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Eagles vs. Cowboys live Date: Monday, Oct. 26 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ET Location: Lincoln Financial Field (Philadelphia) TV: ESPN/ABC | Streaming: Fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Cowboys -4.5, O/U 43.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Cowboys have the ball Dallas has struggled badly on offense over the last two weeks. The Cowboys did total over 300 yards against both the Buccaneers and the Packers, but those totals are misleading. They were entirely unable to deal with blitzes for essentially all of both contests, and that failure brutally undermined their passing attack. ( Dak Prescott , typically excellent against blitzing defenses, went just 20 of 38 for 194 scoreless yards when confronting extra rushers in those games.) They also ran the ball for a mere 98 yards combined in those two games, despite the fact that star guard Tyler Smith returned to the fold. The struggles came a bit as a surprise considering the Cowboys had previously been cooking offensively, racking up yardage and points through the first four weeks of the season. But both Todd Bowles and Jonathan Gannon came out with a plan that toyed with Dallas' protection rules up front, and the Cowboys found themselves unable to respond. They'll need a significantly better plan on Monday night, but it's notable that the Eagles blitz far less often than the Bucs and Packers did against the Cowboys. The Bucs and Packers sent extra rushers after Prescott on 38.8% of his dropbacks in Weeks 5 and 6, per Tru Media. The Eagles have blitzed just 24.1% of the time so far - the fourth-lowest rate in the NFL . Vic Fangio would have to significantly depart from his modus operandi for Philadelphia to employ a strategy similar to the one that dominated Dallas over the last two weeks. For what it's worth, Philly has blitzed on at least 38% of opponent dropbacks just once since Fangio became the team's defensive coordinator. It would be wildly out of character to break out such a strategy here - but it's one worth pursuing considering Dallas' struggles. Philly checks in 20th in opponents' EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, allowing opponents to complete only 60.4% of passes at an average of 7.0 yards per attempt, but giving up eight touchdown passes against just three interceptions and being helped along by 14 opponent drops - second-most in the league. Cornerbacks Quinyon Mitchell , Riq Woolen and Cooper DeJean are tough to beat, but they have also been asked to cover for too long on some dropbacks because of the Eagles' inability to generate pressure. Philly has gotten a sack, hit or hurry on only 32.9% of opponent dropbacks, and they rank below-average in both average time to pressure and average time to throw. Quarterbacks, in other words, have been fairly comfortable in the pocket. And if you let Prescott get comfortable in the pocket, he can pick you apart with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens , among his other targets. The Cowboys seem highly unlikely to find success running the ball, which they haven't done all year. Javonte Williams has seven rushing touchdowns, but he's also averaging only 3.7 yards per carry, down considerably from his 4.8 average last season. The offensive line is not clearing rushing lanes for him, and he's not making anybody miss to make up for it. It's a brutal combination, and with Philly allowing only 4.0 yards per carry, it's not an advantageous one here. When the Eagles have the ball The Eagles enter this game just about as banged up as possible on offense. Quarterback Jalen Hurts is out. His top two receivers, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, are also out. Guard Landon Dickerson remains on injured reserve, though he has been designated to return and listed as questionable for this game. Running back Saquon Barkley is questionable as well, and his top two backups — Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley — are on injured reserve. Without Hurts under center last week, the Eagles operated with a pass-heavy bent. Tanner McKee dropped back to throw 48 times, and while some of that was due to game script and some of it due to Barkley's absence, it's worth noting that he had previously made two Week 18 starts and dropped back to pass an average of 44 times in those games as well. The Eagles can't use the quarterback run game with McKee under center like they can with Hurts, and the rest of their run-game efficiency is likely to suffer as a result of not presenting that threat to the defense. It's somewhat reasonable to expect them to be pass-heavier than we're used to here. That may not be the case if Barkley returns to the lineup, but it is at least somewhat difficult to parse what the Eagles would prefer to do in that situation. Barkley has actually averaged 5.5 yards per carry in each of the two games he's made it through healthy this season. The problem is that the rest of the backs have been extremely inefficient in his absence and he wasn't efficient before leaving the other two games due to injury, either. He fully practiced on Friday for the first time since his hamstring injury, but the team may not want to load him up with too many touches in his first game back in the fold. Every team that is humanly capable of running the football (i.e., not the Texans or Packers) has done so at will against the Cowboys this season, with Dallas' other five opponents each piling up at least 165 yards on the ground. Opponents have clipped the Cowboys for 4.7 yards per carry, with running backs and quarterbacks alike able to find considerable room to run against a disappointingly friendly Dallas front. If the Eagles can get Barkley (or Dameon Pierce ) going early, they might be able to lean on the Cowboys and prevent the game from turning into the kind of track meet that Dallas' offense would prefer. Opponents have also generally been able to throw all over the Cowboys, though it will obviously be difficult for the Eagles to do so while down their top two receivers and multiple of their expected starting offensive linemen. It'll be Makai Lemon , Darius Cooper and Dallas Goedert as McKee's top targets here. It'll be interesting to see if the Cowboys send Joey Porter Jr . to follow one of Cooper (who plays outside) or Lemon (usually in the slot, where he would match up more often with Caleb Downs ), as well as how they align their secondary now that Cobie Durant is set to return and potentially push the struggling (to say it kindly) Daron Bland to the bench. If the Cowboys can put any semblance of pressure on McKee, he could struggle badly. He's just 16 of 45 for 179 scoreless yards in his career when under duress, with a 15.1% sack rate as well. The Cowboys don't rush the passer particularly well, but with the current state of Philly's offensive line, that could change on Monday night. I just don't think the Cowboys should be favored by more than a field goal against anybody right now, given how they're playing on both sides of the ball. I'll take Dallas to win given the state of the Eagles' offense, but I can't see the Cowboys blowing anyone out in their current state. away.blurb: Dallas Goedert is good to go for Monday, while Saquon Barkley and Jalyx Hunt inch closer to a potential return. "It's just kind of the same injury that I sustained earlier. I just had a little bit of inflammation in there, had to let that settle down, but felt really good running out there today," Goedert said after Saturday's practice. "I want to be out there anytime I can. We only get 17 games. To miss a game, to miss two games, it always stinks. So if I can be available, I'm going to do everything I can to play. "I'm going to go out there and do whatever I can to help the team win, whether it's run blocking, pass blocking, or hopefully get a couple catches. We're looking forward to this game playing on Monday night against the division rival. It's going to be a lot of fun. The atmosphere's going to be great and it's a game I wouldn't want to miss." Two of the Eagles' top receivers, DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), have been ruled out, leaving rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon as the primary wide receiver option. "It's definitely a big opportunity with the team," Lemon said. "I'm just super excited to go out there with the guys, put on a good performance. Had a great week of practice with all the guys. So, just trying to go out there and execute. A couple guys are out. So really just, next man up. I got a bunch of trust in the guys next to me, trust in the coaches and the game plan." The running back is listed as questionable for Monday night. Meanwhile, Jonathan Greenard (ankle), who did not practice again on Saturday, is listed as questionable. The edge rusher said it will be a game-time decision as he will need to see how his ankle feels. Alongside Greenard, the outside linebacker room is banged up. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) could return on Monday as he is listed as questionable after practicing in a limited capacity all week. Nolan Smith (concussion) has been officially ruled out. Smith is joined by defensive back Michael Carter II (abdomen). Cornerback Jakorian Bennett, tight end Grant Calcaterra, guard Landon Dickerson, and tight end Eli Stowers all participated fully in practice on Saturday. They are all listed as questionable since they are on Injured Reserve and would need to be activated by Monday afternoon in order to play against the Cowboys. away.blurb: Running back Saquon Barkley is on track to appear for the first time since leaving the Week 4 game early, and should bring a huge boost to a running game that has floundered the last three weeks. Hopefully ready to meet him in the hole is linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who hasn't seen action since Week 1 for the Cowboys. The Cowboys also expect CB Cobie Durant to return to action, and he hasn't played since Week 2. Those are two big additions for Dallas. Things are trending right for several other Cowboys, though they aren't quite ready to return to action. The Cowboys opened the 21-day practice window for LB Marist Liufau and safety PJ Locke. Both were expected to be key reserves this year and still could be activated before Monday's game, with corresponding roster moves. Starting safety Jalen Thompson can have his window opened next week. Meanwhile, Dallas did rule out WR/KR Kavontae Turpin (ribs) and LB Dee Winters (calf), along with OT Drew Shelton. McKee won't have his top two receivers as both DeVonta Smith and Dontarin Wycks have been ruled out. Barkley is one of seven listed as questionable, along with OF Landon Dickerson and edge rusher Jonathan Greenard, who is expected to be a game-time decision . Entering their Week 7 Monday Night Football matchup, the teams sport identical 2-4 records after six games , with injuries the underlying factor of both club's malaise. Dallas, implementing a new defense under first-year coordinator Christian Parker, has seen their back-seven progressively decimated week by week, undermining his attempt to get his footing as a scheme designer and playcaller. The Eagles have just lost body after body throughout their roster, losing key contributors to the offense. Are the clubs trending in opposite directions despite losing streaks for both ? Injury wise, Dallas is starting to get some contributors back, with the question being about whether they can actually make a difference or is Parker's scheme a bad one. The Eagles are trending down, still, though they will get a big boost from one returning member. For Philly, the injury discussion has centered around QB Jalen Hurts and the controversy over his blood clot diagnosis . Regardless of the inner workings there, he's been moved to IR and is done for the year, opening the door for Tanner McKee to get the start and raising the possibility if he flounders, the Eagles could turn to Joe Milton III at QB. home.headline: Is Saquon Barkley playing today? Eagles injury report with RB on the mend
home.blurb: The season feels like it's on the line for the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7 now that Jalen Hurts is out for the season. The ever-forgiving NFC East could keep the Eagles afloat for a bit, but they need to score a win against the Dallas Cowboys on Monday night to keep pace in a wide-open division. The official word on Barkley is expected closer to game time, but all signs are pointing towards the Pro Bowler making his official return in Week 7. The Eagles listed Barkley as questionable but he did practice in full on Saturday, with NFL Network's Ian Rapoport noting that the expectation is for Barkley to take the field on Monday. The fact that this is a Monday night game without a clear call makes life quite difficult for managers with Barkley on their roster. The upside that Barkley offers is enormous, but if he is ruled out prior to the game there are few legitimate alternatives to plug in for him. The good news for Barkley backers is that the Eagles will likely give him everything he can handle if he's active. Both DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks are out for this game, leaving Dallas Goedert and Makai Lemon as the top receiving weapons for backup QB Tanner McKee. It would be a big help if Philly can get running back Saquon Barkley on the field for that pivotal matchup. The good news is that Barkley, who has been sidelined since suffering a hamstring injury in Week 5 against the Los Angeles Rams , does appear to be trending in the right direction. Is Saquon Barkley playing today? What Eagles are saying about RB1's role in Week 7 It isn't clear yet if Barkley will assume the full starting workload for the Eagles, but it would make sense for Philadelphia to give him some kind of help given the fact he is coming off a hamstring injury. It would be quite helpful for Nick Sirianni, however, if Barkley can take as much work as possible on Monday. There isn't much on the Eagles' depth chart behind Saquon Barkley Injuries have been quite the theme for the Eagles' backfield this season. Besides Barkley, they lost Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley to injured reserve already this season. That is not a misprint, as Barkley would join Dameon Pierce as the only healthy running backs on Philadelphia's roster. The Eagles do have two running backs, Jaydon Blue and Elijah Mitchell, on their practice squad and will likely elevate one of them to the active roster prior to Monday night's game to give themselves an insurance policy in case Barkley's hamstring acts up. What to expect from Saquon Barkley in fantasy football for Week 7 If Pierce is still on waiver wires, that should be the priority for those planning to roll with Barkley. It would be smart to proactively add Blue and/or Mitchell for those locking Barkley into an RB spot, while a FLEX spot does open more possibilities. That leaves rookie Makai Lemon as the top option and tight end Dallas Goedert (17 catches, 180 yards) as the safety valve for a quarterback who went 26-of-45 for 215 yards against Carolina. Opponents convert 54.7% of their third downs against the Cowboys, the worst mark in the league, and Dallas has forced only three turnovers. The third-down struggles showed up again in Green Bay, where the Packers went 11-of-18. Dallas has allowed at least 20 points in 13 straight games, a franchise record. home.headline: Cowboys vs. Eagles Injury Report
home.blurb: Dallas Goedert is good to go for Monday, while Saquon Barkley and Jalyx Hunt inch closer to a potential return. "It's just kind of the same injury that I sustained earlier. I just had a little bit of inflammation in there, had to let that settle down, but felt really good running out there today," Goedert said after Saturday's practice. "I want to be out there anytime I can. We only get 17 games. To miss a game, to miss two games, it always stinks. So if I can be available, I'm going to do everything I can to play. "I'm going to go out there and do whatever I can to help the team win, whether it's run blocking, pass blocking, or hopefully get a couple catches. We're looking forward to this game playing on Monday night against the division rival. It's going to be a lot of fun. The atmosphere's going to be great and it's a game I wouldn't want to miss." Two of the Eagles' top receivers, DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), have been ruled out, leaving rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon as the primary wide receiver option. "It's definitely a big opportunity with the team," Lemon said. "I'm just super excited to go out there with the guys, put on a good performance. Had a great week of practice with all the guys. So, just trying to go out there and execute. A couple guys are out. So really just, next man up. I got a bunch of trust in the guys next to me, trust in the coaches and the game plan." Running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) took a step forward and was a full participant at practice on Saturday after being limited previously in the week. The running back is listed as questionable for Monday night. Meanwhile, Jonathan Greenard (ankle), who did not practice again on Saturday, is listed as questionable. The edge rusher said it will be a game-time decision as he will need to see how his ankle feels. Alongside Greenard, the outside linebacker room is banged up. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) could return on Monday as he is listed as questionable after practicing in a limited capacity all week. Nolan Smith (concussion) has been officially ruled out. Smith is joined by defensive back Michael Carter II (abdomen). Cornerback Jakorian Bennett, tight end Grant Calcaterra, guard Landon Dickerson, and tight end Eli Stowers all participated fully in practice on Saturday. They are all listed as questionable since they are on Injured Reserve and would need to be activated by Monday afternoon in order to play against the Cowboys.
